claims.claim: Treatment with tunicamycin or tfg-1 RNAi specifically induces ER stress.
claims.source: Both treatments specifically induce ER stress (Levi-Ferber et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work by the same authors.

claims.claim: CED-1::GFP-engulfed apoptotic corpses were only detected in tumorous gonads upon induction of ER stress.
claims.source: CED-1::GFP-engulfed apoptotic corpses were only detected in tumorous gonads upon induction of ER stress.
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data using the CED-1::GFP marker.

claims.claim: GLD-1 protein levels were similarly reduced in animals treated with gld-1 RNAi along with control RNAi or tfg-1 RNAi.
claims.source: These differences were not the result of restoration of gld-1 expression in the stressed animals as GLD-1 protein levels were similarly reduced in animals treated with gld-1 RNAi along with control RNAi or tfg-1 RNAi (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in the figure supplement.

claims.claim: In non-tumorous gonads, apoptotic germ cell corpses are usually detected at the turn of the gonad where oogenesis occurs.
claims.source: First, in terms of location within the gonad—whereas in non-tumorous gonads apoptotic germ cell corpses were usually detected at the turn of the gonad, where oogenesis occurs, those detected in ER-stressed tumorous gonads were located in the proximal region of the gonad (Figure 1A,D).
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental observations shown in the figures.

claims.claim: Apoptotic corpses in ER-stressed tumorous gonads are located in the proximal region of the gonad.
claims.source: First, in terms of location within the gonad—whereas in non-tumorous gonads apoptotic germ cell corpses were usually detected at the turn of the gonad, where oogenesis occurs, those detected in ER-stressed tumorous gonads were located in the proximal region of the gonad (Figure 1A,D).
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental observations shown in the figures.

claims.claim: SYTO12-labeled nuclei and CED-1::GFP-engulfed cells in tumorous gonads exposed to ER stress were significantly larger than those detected in non-tumorous animals.
claims.source: In addition, in terms of size, both the SYTO12-labeled nuclei and the CED-1::GFP-engulfed cells in the tumorous gonads exposed to ER stress were significantly larger than those detected in non-tumorous animals (Figure 1A,C,D,E).
claims.evidence: This is supported by quantitative data shown in the figures.

claims.claim: CED-1::GFP engulfed cells in ER-stressed tumorous gonads displayed a variety of shapes, unlike the typically round engulfed germ cell corpses.
claims.source: Furthermore, unlike engulfed germ cell corpses that are typically round, the CED-1::GFP engulfed cells in the ER-stressed tumorous gonads displayed a variety of shapes (Figure 1D).
claims.evidence: This is supported by microscopy observations shown in the figure.

claims.claim: The apoptotic cell corpses in ER-stressed tumorous gonads are distinct from the germ cell corpses observed in non-tumorous gonads.
claims.source: Altogether, the differences in size, shape and location suggest that the apoptotic cell corpses in ER-stressed tumorous gonads are distinct from the germ cell corpses observed in non-tumorous gonads.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the observed differences in size, shape, and location.

claims.claim: Blocking apoptosis by ced-3 inactivation resulted in the accumulation of cells with large and misshaped nuclei occupying nearly 40% of the ER-stressed gonad.
claims.source: Strikingly, blocking apoptosis resulted in the accumulation of cells with large and misshaped nuclei occupying nearly 40% of the stressed gonad (Figure 2A,B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by quantitative data from DAPI staining shown in the figures.

claims.claim: In the absence of ER stress, blocking apoptosis resulted in the accumulation of ectopic cells with large and misshaped nuclei occupying only 10% of the gonad in gld-1 RNAi-treated animals.
claims.source: However, in the absence of ER stress, the abnormally large nuclei occupied only 10% of the gonad (Figure 2A,B), indicating that ER stress promotes their induction.
claims.evidence: This is supported by quantitative data shown in the figures.

claims.claim: ER stress promotes the induction of ectopic cells with large nuclei in gld-1-deficient animals.
claims.source: However, in the absence of ER stress, the abnormally large nuclei occupied only 10% of the gonad (Figure 2A,B), indicating that ER stress promotes their induction.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the comparison of ectopic cell accumulation with and without ER stress.

claims.claim: Blocking apoptosis enabled the detection of ectopic cells within the gonads of nearly 90% of the gld-1 RNAi-treated animals examined, both under normal growth conditions and under ER stress.
claims.source: Interestingly, blocking apoptosis enabled the detection of ectopic cells within the gonads of nearly 90% of the gld-1 RNAi-treated animals examined, both under normal growth conditions as well as under ER stress, albeit to different extents (Figure 2—figure supplement 1 and Figure 2A,B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by quantitative data shown in the figure supplement.

claims.claim: Treatment of gld-1(q485); ced-3(n1286) double mutants with tfg-1 RNAi increased the accumulation of cells with large nuclei in the gonads.
claims.source: Furthermore, treatment of gld-1(q485); ced-3(n1286) double mutants with ER-stress inducing tfg-1 RNAi also increased the accumulation of cells with large nuclei in the gonads (Figure 2C), recapitulating the phenomena observed in gld-1, tfg-1 and ced-3 RNAi-treated animals.
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in the figure.

claims.claim: ire-1 is not required for germ cell transdifferentiation per se, but is required for germ cell transdifferentiation in response to ER stress.
claims.source: We conclude that ire-1 is not required for germ cell transdifferentiation per se. However, it is required for germ cell transdifferentiation in response to ER stress.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the observation that basal transdifferentiation occurs in ire-1 mutants but ER stress-induced enhancement does not.

claims.claim: The regulation of germ cell pluripotency by ER stress in gld-1-deficient animals requires the activation of the ER stress sensor IRE-1.
claims.source: Furthermore, these findings indicate that the regulation of germ cell pluripotency by ER stress in gld-1-deficient animals requires the activation of the ER stress sensor IRE-1, and is not simply the result of interference with ER homeostasis and function.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the genetic requirement for ire-1 in ER stress-induced transdifferentiation.

claims.claim: Genetically-induced ER stress resulted in a 3-6 fold increase in the fluorescence of each of the three germ layer transgenic markers in tumorous gonads.
claims.source: Genetically-induced ER stress resulted in a 3–6 fold increase in the fluorescence of each of the three germ layers transgenic markers in the tumorous gonads (Figure 3A).
claims.evidence: This is supported by quantitative fluorescence data shown in the figure.

claims.claim: Treatment with tunicamycin increased the fluorescence of the neuronal marker Punc-119::gfp in the tumorous gonads of gld-1; ced-3 deficient animals.
claims.source: Similarly, treatment with tunicamycin increased the fluorescence of the neuronal marker Punc-119::gfp in the tumorous gonads of gld-1; ced-3 deficient animals (Figure 3B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in the figure.

claims.claim: Ectopic somatic cells were not detected in the gonad of germ cell-deficient glp-1 animals upon induction of ER stress.
claims.source: Ectopic somatic cells were not detected in the gonad of germ cell-deficient glp-1 animals, although they were detected in control germ cell (+) animals upon induction of ER stress (Figure 3C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in the figure.

claims.claim: The ectopic somatic cells induced by ER stress in the tumorous gonad are derived from the germ cells themselves.
claims.source: These findings are consistent with the possibility that the ectopic somatic cells induced by ER stress in the tumorous gonad are derived from the germ cells themselves, uncovering ER stress as a potent regulator of germ cell pluripotency.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the absence of ectopic cells in germ cell-deficient animals.

claims.claim: ER stress acts as a potent regulator of germ cell pluripotency.
claims.source: These findings are consistent with the possibility that the ectopic somatic cells induced by ER stress in the tumorous gonad are derived from the germ cells themselves, uncovering ER stress as a potent regulator of germ cell pluripotency.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the experimental findings showing ER stress-induced transdifferentiation.

claims.claim: Previously identified regulators of germ cell pluripotency act at the final steps of the transdifferentiation process by directly regulating gene expression.
claims.source: Importantly, unlike previously identified regulators of germ cell pluripotency, all of which act at the final steps of the transdifferentiation process by directly regulating gene expression (Ciosk et al., 2006; Tursun et al., 2011; Patel et al., 2012; Updike et al., 2014); ER stress and ER homeostasis likely act further upstream, linking between cellular and organismal physiology and germ cell fate.
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claims.claim: ER stress and ER homeostasis likely act upstream of previously identified regulators, linking cellular and organismal physiology to germ cell fate.
claims.source: Importantly, unlike previously identified regulators of germ cell pluripotency, all of which act at the final steps of the transdifferentiation process by directly regulating gene expression (Ciosk et al., 2006; Tursun et al., 2011; Patel et al., 2012; Updike et al., 2014); ER stress and ER homeostasis likely act further upstream, linking between cellular and organismal physiology and germ cell fate.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the comparison with previously identified regulators.

claims.claim: tfg-1 RNAi failed to increase germ cell transdifferentiation in ire-1-deficient animals.
claims.source: In contrast, tfg-1 RNAi failed to increase germ cell transdifferentiation in ire-1-deficient animals (Figure 4A).
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in the figure.

claims.claim: A low level of ectopic somatic cells was detected in gld-1; ire-1-deficient animals, similar to that observed in gld-1-deficient animals not exposed to ER stress.
claims.source: Nevertheless, a low level of ectopic somatic cells, similar to that observed in gld-1-deficient animals that were not exposed to ER stress, was still detected in gld-1; ire-1-deficient animals (Figure 4A).
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in the figure.

claims.claim: The basal level of germ cell transdifferentiation in gld-1; ire-1-deficient animals was not increased by tfg-1 RNAi-induced ER stress or by the ER stress associated with ire-1 deficiency.
claims.source: This basal level of germ cell transdifferentiation was not increased by tfg-1 RNAi-induced ER stress or by the ER stress associated with the ire-1 deficiency.
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental observations in ire-1 mutants.

claims.claim: Significantly increased levels of ectopic nuclei were detected in the gonads of both xbp-1(zc12) and xbp-1(tm2457) mutants upon treatment with gld-1 and ced-3 RNAi on day 4 of adulthood.
claims.source: Strikingly, we detected significantly increased levels of ectopic nuclei in the gonads of both xbp-1 mutants upon treatment with a mixture of gld-1 and ced-3 RNAi on day 4 of adulthood (Figure 4B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in the figure.

claims.claim: Deficiency in XBP1 leads to activation of the ER stress sensor IRE1 in mice and C. elegans xbp-1(zc12) mutants.
claims.source: Previous studies in mice and in C. elegans xbp-1(zc12) mutants have demonstrated that the mere deficiency in XBP1 leads to activation of the ER stress sensor IRE1 (Hu et al., 2009; Richardson et al., 2011; Hur et al., 2012; Safra et al., 2013)
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claims.claim: The high level of germ cell transdifferentiation in xbp-1 mutants was completely dependent on ire-1.
claims.source: Consistent with this interpretation, the high level of germ cell transdifferentiation in xbp-1 mutants was completely dependent on ire-1 (Figure 4B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing no transdifferentiation in xbp-1; ire-1 double mutants.

claims.claim: ER stress-induced germ cell transdifferentiation is completely dependent on ire-1 but not dependent on xbp-1.
claims.source: Thus, although ER stress-induced germ cell transdifferentiation is completely dependent on the ER stress sensor gene ire-1, it is not dependent on its downstream target xbp-1, implying that it is mediated by an ire-1-dependent xbp-1-independent signal.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the genetic epistasis experiments.

claims.claim: ER stress-induced germ cell transdifferentiation is mediated by an ire-1-dependent xbp-1-independent signal.
claims.source: Thus, although ER stress-induced germ cell transdifferentiation is completely dependent on the ER stress sensor gene ire-1, it is not dependent on its downstream target xbp-1, implying that it is mediated by an ire-1-dependent xbp-1-independent signal.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the genetic data showing ire-1 requirement but not xbp-1 requirement.

claims.claim: xbp-1 inactivation suppressed the germline tumor in gld-1-deficient animals.
claims.source: We found that xbp-1 inactivation, not only induced germ cell transdifferentiation but also suppressed the germline tumor; demonstrating that the two phenomena are tightly correlated.
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental observations of tumor phenotypes in xbp-1 mutants.

claims.claim: Germ cell transdifferentiation and tumor suppression are tightly correlated.
claims.source: We found that xbp-1 inactivation, not only induced germ cell transdifferentiation but also suppressed the germline tumor; demonstrating that the two phenomena are tightly correlated.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the observation that both phenomena occur together.

claims.claim: The density of germ cells in the germline tumor was reduced in tumorous animals exposed to ER stress such that the germline tumor did not fill the entire gonad.
claims.source: The physiological improvement was manifested in several ways: (a) the density of the germ cells in the germline tumor was reduced in the tumorous animals exposed to ER stress such that the germline tumor that occupied the proximal gonad did not fill the entire gonad (Figure 5A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is supported by microscopy observations shown in the figures.

claims.claim: ER stress significantly delayed the paralysis of tumorous animals and allowed them to move freely at time-points where most non-stressed tumorous animals were paralyzed.
claims.source: We find that ER stress significantly delayed the paralysis of the tumorous animals and allowed the animals to move freely at time-points where most of the non-stressed tumorous animals were paralyzed (Figure 5B, Videos 1, 2 and Figure 5—Figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: This is supported by paralysis assay data shown in the figures and videos.

claims.claim: Treatment with gld-1 RNAi shortened the lifespan of wild-type animals by more than 30%, whereas it shortened the lifespan of ER stressed-xbp-1 mutants by only 13%.
claims.source: We found that in wild-type animals, treatment with gld-1 RNAi shortened the lifespan by more than 30%, whereas it shortened the lifespan of ER stressed-xbp-1 mutants by only 13% (Figure 5C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by lifespan analysis data shown in the figure.

claims.claim: Treatment with gld-1 RNAi shortened wild-type animals lifespan by more than 30%, whereas it shortened the lifespan of tfg-1 RNAi-treated animals by only 15%.
claims.source: Similarly, treatment with gld-1 RNAi shortened wild-type animals lifespan by more than 30%, whereas it shortened the lifespan of tfg-1 RNAi-treated animals by only 15% (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by lifespan analysis data shown in the figure supplement.

claims.claim: No physiological improvement in terms of lifespan, movement or germline density were observed in ire-1 deficient animals upon xbp-1 inactivation.
claims.source: Importantly, no physiological improvement in terms of lifespan, movement or germline density were observed in ire-1 deficient animals, in which ER stress-induced germ cell transdifferentiation does not occur, even upon xbp-1 inactivation (Figure 5 and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in the figures.

claims.claim: The genetic requirements for suppression of the germline tumor and for induction of germ cell transdifferentiation converge on ire-1.
claims.source: Thus, the genetic requirements for suppression of the germline tumor and for induction of germ cell transdifferentiation converge on ire-1.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the observation that both processes require ire-1.

claims.claim: DNA damage, pathogens, oxidative, osmotic, heat shock, starvation and ER stress are all known inducers of germ cell apoptosis in normal (non-tumorous) germlines.
claims.source: DNA damage, pathogens, oxidative, osmotic, heat shock, starvation and ER stress are all known inducers of germ cell apoptosis in normal (i.e., non-tumorous) germlines (Gartner et al., 2000; Salinas et al., 2006; Levi-Ferber et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claims.claim: Only treatment with tfg-1 RNAi led to the detection of cells with large nuclei in the gonads of gld-1; ced-3-deficient animals, although some treatments induced more germ cell apoptosis than tfg-1 RNAi.
claims.source: We found that although some treatments induced more germ cell apoptosis than tfg-1 RNAi, only treatment with tfg-1 RNAi led to the detection of cells with large nuclei in the gonads of gld-1; ced-3-deficient animals (Figure 6B and black bar graphs).
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data comparing different stress treatments shown in the figure.

claims.claim: The transdifferentiation of germ cells is not simply a side-effect or default fate of apoptosis-resistant tumorous cells under proapoptotic stress.
claims.source: This indicates that the transdifferentiation of the germ cells is not simply a side-effect or a default fate of apoptosis-resistant tumorous cells under proapoptotic stress which they fail to execute.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the specificity of ER stress in inducing transdifferentiation compared to other stresses.

claims.claim: Only treatment with tfg-1 RNAi suppressed the progression of the germline tumor among the tested stresses.
claims.source: Moreover, since only treatment with tfg-1 RNAi suppressed the progression of the germline tumor (Figure 6—figure supplement 1), this lends further support to the notion that induction of germ cell transdifferentiation is a prerequisite for the suppression of the germline tumor.
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in the figure supplement.

claims.claim: Induction of germ cell transdifferentiation is a prerequisite for the suppression of the germline tumor.
claims.source: Moreover, since only treatment with tfg-1 RNAi suppressed the progression of the germline tumor (Figure 6—figure supplement 1), this lends further support to the notion that induction of germ cell transdifferentiation is a prerequisite for the suppression of the germline tumor.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the correlation between transdifferentiation and tumor suppression.

claims.claim: ER stress is beneficial for the healthspan of gld-1-deficient animals as it suppresses their lethal germline tumors.
claims.source: We find that while severe stress limits organismal survival and well-being under most circumstances, ER stress is beneficial for the animals' healthspan in gld-1-deficient animals, as it suppresses their lethal germline tumors.
claims.evidence: This is supported by the lifespan, paralysis, and tumor density data.

claims.claim: Knockout of hsf1 in mice has deleterious impact on organismal survival under normal growth conditions and under stress, but benefits the organism in the case of cancer.
claims.source: This is in accordance with previous findings that a stress-inducing interference such as knockout of hsf1 in mice, which has deleterious impact on organismal survival under normal growth conditions as well as under stress, actually benefits the same organism in the case of cancer (Dai et al., 2007).
claims.evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claims.claim: The suppression of the germline tumor is the combined effect of germ cell transdifferentiation coupled with a limited half-life of the transdifferentiated germ cells.
claims.source: Our findings indicate that the suppression of the germline tumor is the combined effect of germ cell transdifferentiation coupled with a limited half-life of the transdifferentiated germ cells (see model in Figure 7).
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the experimental observations and presented as a model.

claims.claim: The limited half-life of transdifferentiated germ cells is achieved by restoring their responsiveness to apoptosis once they transdifferentiate into ectopic somatic cells.
claims.source: The latter is achieved by restoring the responsiveness of the tumorous cells to apoptosis once they transdifferentiate into ectopic somatic cells and the subsequent removal of their ectopic somatic corpses from the gonad.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the observation that transdifferentiated cells undergo apoptosis.

claims.claim: Although germ cell transdifferentiation normally occurs in gld-1-deficient animals, its extent is not sufficient to effectively suppress the tumor by itself.
claims.source: Importantly, although germ cell transdifferentiation normally occurs in gld-1-deficient animals (Ciosk et al., 2006), its extent is not sufficient to effectively suppress the tumor by itself.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the comparison of basal and ER stress-induced transdifferentiation levels and their effects on tumor progression.

claims.claim: Effective tumor suppression is only achieved under conditions that further enhance germ cell transdifferentiation beyond its basal level, as in the case of ER stress.
claims.source: Effective suppression is only achieved under conditions that further enhance germ cell transdifferentiation beyond its basal level, as in the case of ER stress.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the experimental observations comparing basal and enhanced transdifferentiation.

claims.claim: Tumor cell transdifferentiation may serve as a protective anti-tumor mechanism.
claims.source: All in all, our results indicate that tumor cell transdifferentiation may serve as a protective anti-tumor mechanism.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the experimental findings showing tumor suppression through transdifferentiation.

claims.claim: Transdifferentiation-promoting genes may effectively suppress tumors.
claims.source: This implies that transdifferentiation-promoting genes may effectively suppress tumors.
claims.evidence: This is speculated based on the findings that transdifferentiation suppresses tumors.

claims.claim: A major consequence of ER stress is interference with ER functions, which may directly impinge upon the production of signaling molecules such as secreted peptides, hormones, cholesterol and lipids.
claims.source: A major consequence of ER stress is interference with ER functions, which may directly impinge upon the production of a variety of signaling molecules such as secreted peptides, hormones, cholesterol and lipids which are metabolized in the ER.
claims.evidence: This is based on established knowledge of ER function.

claims.claim: It is unlikely that interference with ER functions directly accounts for ER stress-induced germline transdifferentiation and apoptosis because these do not occur in animals under severe ER stress in the absence of ire-1.
claims.source: However, it is unlikely that this directly accounts for ER stress-induced germline transdifferentiation and apoptosis of the germ cells as these do not occur in animals under severe ER stress in the absence of ire-1.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the genetic requirement for ire-1.

claims.claim: It is the activation of the ER stress sensor IRE-1, rather than a non-specific consequence of ER stress per se, that regulates germ cell pro-differentiation and tumor progression in gld-1-deficient animals.
claims.source: This suggests that it is the activation of the ER stress sensor IRE-1, rather than a non-specific consequence of ER stress per se, that regulate germ cell pro-differentiation and tumor progression in gld-1-deficient animals.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the genetic requirement for ire-1 and independence from xbp-1.

claims.claim: Germ-cell transdifferentiation is mediated by an ire-1-dependent xbp-1 independent signal.
claims.source: Furthermore, since germ-cell transdifferentiation is promoted in animal deficient in xbp-1, this indicates that it is mediated by an ire-1-dependent xbp-1 independent signal.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the genetic epistasis experiments.

claims.claim: In humans, mutations that compromise the activity or expression of RNase L have been implicated with increased susceptibility to prostate cancer.
claims.source: Interestingly, in humans, mutations that compromise the activity or the expression of RNase L, an IRE1-related endoribonuclease, have been implicated with increased susceptibility to prostate cancer (Carpten et al., 2002; Casey et al., 2002).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claims.claim: RNase L is an IRE1-related endoribonuclease that has lost specificity to xbp-1 mRNA but shares with IRE-1 its promiscuous RNase activity.
claims.source: Unlike IRE1, RNase L has lost specificity to xbp-1 mRNA. Nevertheless, it shares with IRE-1 its promiscuous RNase activity.
claims.evidence: This is based on established knowledge of RNase L and IRE-1 biochemistry.

claims.claim: Tumor-suppressive properties of IRE-1-related endoribonucleases may be evolutionarily conserved.
claims.source: This implies that tumor-suppressive properties of IRE-1-related endoribonucleases may be evolutionarily conserved, and may not be specifically associated with one specific type of prostate cancer.
claims.evidence: This is speculated based on the similarity between IRE-1 and RNase L and their tumor-suppressive properties.

claims.claim: One hallmark of aggressive tumors is their adaptation to their natural primary niche.
claims.source: One hallmark of aggressive tumors is their adaptation to their natural primary niche (Hanahan and Weinberg, 2000, 2011).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to cancer biology literature.

claims.claim: Transformation into an ectopic kind of cell may have added value in suppressing aggressive tumors compared to differentiation into a cell type normally found in the same primary niche.
claims.source: Thus, transformation into an ectopic kind of cell, rather than differentiation into a type of cell which can normally be found in the same primary niche, may have an added value in suppressing aggressive tumors.
claims.evidence: This is speculated based on the concept of niche adaptation.

claims.claim: In 95% of human ovarian germline tumors, totipotent germ cells precociously differentiate into a variety of ectopic somatic cells generating teratoma.
claims.source: Strikingly, in 95% of human ovarian germline tumors, the totipotent germ cells precociously differentiate into a variety of ectopic somatic cells generating teratoma (Koonings et al., 1989; Ulbright, 2005).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to clinical literature.

claims.claim: Naturally occurring teratomas are usually benign whereas the remaining 5% of human ovarian germline tumors are usually malignant.
claims.source: These naturally occurring teratoma are usually benign whereas the remaining 5% are usually malignant (Ulbright, 2005).
claims.evidence: This is supported by a citation to clinical literature.

claims.claim: Teratoma may be a preferential germline tumor in terms of survival and fitness of the organism.
claims.source: This suggests that teratoma may be a preferential germline tumor in terms of survival and fitness of the organism.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the observation that most ovarian germline tumors are benign teratomas.

claims.claim: Some ovarian teratomas undergo malignant transformation, but this occurs only in 1.5% of teratomas.
claims.source: Accordingly, some of the ovarian teratoma undergo a malignant transformation which occurs after the development of the teratoma. Nevertheless, this occurs only in 1.5% of teratoma (Comerci et al., 1994; Ayhan et al., 2000; Ulbright, 2005).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to clinical literature.

claims.claim: The conclusions from the C. elegans tumor model are naturally applied to human germline tumor biology.
claims.source: This suggests that the conclusions derived from our studies in the C. elegans tumor model system are already naturally applied for human germline tumor biology, as if they were selected to do so by evolution.
claims.evidence: This is speculated based on the similarity between the C. elegans findings and human teratoma biology.

claims.claim: The potential to suppress tumors by forcing their transdifferentiation requires the tumor cells to have differentiation potential.
claims.source: The potential to suppress tumors by forcing their transdifferentiation requires the tumor cells to have differentiation potential.
claims.evidence: This is a logical inference from the concept of transdifferentiation-mediated tumor suppression.

claims.claim: In mammals, subpopulations of stem cells that maintain differentiation potential exist in many organs and tissues, albeit at low numbers.
claims.source: In mammals, in addition to the totipotent germ cells, subpopulations of stem cells, which maintain differentiation potential (i.e., pluri or multi-potent) exist in many organs and tissues, albeit at low numbers (Reya et al., 2001).
claims.evidence: This is supported by a citation to stem cell biology literature.

claims.claim: Within tumors and hematological cancers, one can find a subpopulation of cancer stem cells that possess stem cell characteristics, including the ability to give rise to a variety of cell types.
claims.source: Furthermore, within tumors and hematological cancers, one can find a subpopulation of cancer stem cells that possess stem cells characteristics, including the ability to give rise to a variety of cell types (Reya et al., 2001).
claims.evidence: This is supported by a citation to cancer stem cell literature.

claims.claim: Differentiation therapy has been used in the clinic and is proven to be effective in limiting some kinds of tumors.
claims.source: Accordingly, differentiation therapy has been used in the clinic and is proven to be effective in limiting some kinds of tumors (Sell, 2004).
claims.evidence: This is supported by a citation to clinical literature.

claims.claim: Current differentiation therapies induce differentiation of cells within the same lineage.
claims.source: Interestingly, whereas these treatments induce differentiation of cells within the same lineage, induction of transdifferentiation into a completely different cellular lineage may be even more effective by creating a discrepancy and maladaptiveness between the tumorous cells and their surrounding niche.
claims.evidence: This is stated as a contrast to the proposed transdifferentiation approach.

claims.claim: Induction of transdifferentiation into a completely different cellular lineage may be more effective than same-lineage differentiation by creating discrepancy between tumorous cells and their surrounding niche.
claims.source: Interestingly, whereas these treatments induce differentiation of cells within the same lineage, induction of transdifferentiation into a completely different cellular lineage may be even more effective by creating a discrepancy and maladaptiveness between the tumorous cells and their surrounding niche.
claims.evidence: This is speculated based on the concept of niche adaptation.

claims.claim: Induction of tumor cell transdifferentiation has the potential to be applied as a novel approach to combat cancer and overcome the escape of tumor cells from the cell death machinery in a wide variety of tissues.
claims.source: Thus, induction of tumor cell transdifferentiation has the potential to be applied as a novel approach to combat cancer and overcome the escape of tumor cells from the cell death machinery in a wide variety of tissues.
claims.evidence: This is speculated based on the experimental findings and their potential therapeutic implications.

claims.claim: Under ER stress conditions, cells that expressed the neuronal marker co-localized with cells in the gonad that had atypically large nuclei.
claims.source: We found that under ER stress conditions, the cells that expressed the neuronal marker co-localized with the cells in the gonad that had atypically large nuclei.
claims.evidence: This is supported by co-localization experiments shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: No expression of the Punc-119::gfp somatic marker was detected in regions of the gonad devoid of large-nucleated cells.
claims.source: No expression of the Punc-119::gfp somatic marker was detected in regions of the gonad devoid of large-nucleated cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: This is supported by microscopy observations shown in the figure supplement.

claims.claim: Some of the engulfed cells in the stressed tumorous gonad also expressed the somatic marker.
claims.source: Indeed, some of the engulfed cells also expressed the somatic marker (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by co-expression experiments shown in the figure supplement.

claims.claim: The ectopic somatic cells that arise in the stressed tumorous gonad normally undergo apoptosis and are consequently engulfed and cleared from the gonad.
claims.source: These findings are consistent with the interpretation that the ectopic somatic cells that arise in the stressed tumorous gonad normally undergo apoptosis and are consequently engulfed and cleared from the gonad.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the observation of engulfed cells expressing somatic markers.

claims.claim: The teratoma contains somatic cells of different germ-layers, so only a fraction can be detected using somatic markers of specific tissues or germ layers.
claims.source: Why was the expression of the intestinal somatic marker apparent only in some of the ced-1::gfp labeled phagosomes and not in all of them? Likewise, why weren't all the large-nucleated cells co-localized with the cells in the gonad that expressed the neuronal marker? These phenomena are likely the consequence of the fact that the teratoma contains somatic cells of the different germ-layers, implying that only a fraction of the teratoma cells can be detected using somatic markers of specific tissues or germ layers.
claims.evidence: This is inferred to explain why not all ectopic cells express a given somatic marker.

results.result: ER stress induces apoptosis in apoptosis-resistant gld-1-deficient tumorous germ cells. The apoptotic corpses detected in ER-stressed tumorous gonads differ from typical germ cell corpses in size, shape, and location, suggesting they represent a distinct cell population.
results.evaluation: Claims C17-C18 and C22 provide direct experimental evidence using SYTO12 and CED-1::GFP markers showing apoptotic corpses only appear upon ER stress induction. Claims C24-C28 document distinct morphological and spatial characteristics of these corpses. Claim C23 controls for GLD-1 protein levels, ruling out restoration of gld-1 expression as an explanation. The convergence of multiple independent markers and quantitative measurements strongly supports this result.

results.result: Blocking apoptosis by ced-3 inactivation results in accumulation of ectopic cells with large, misshaped nuclei in gld-1-deficient gonads. ER stress significantly enhances this accumulation (from ~10% to ~40% of gonad area), indicating ER stress promotes the generation of these ectopic cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C29-C30 provide quantitative DAPI staining data showing differential accumulation with and without ER stress. Claim C32 demonstrates high penetrance (~90%) of the phenotype. Claim C33 validates findings in genetic mutants, ruling out RNAi artifacts. The dose-response relationship between ER stress and ectopic cell accumulation, combined with genetic validation, strongly supports this result.

results.result: The ectopic cells with large nuclei in ER-stressed gld-1-deficient gonads express somatic differentiation markers from all three germ layers. These somatic marker-expressing cells co-localize with large-nucleated cells and are found among CED-1::GFP-engulfed cells, indicating they undergo apoptosis and clearance.
results.evaluation: Claims C36-C37 provide quantitative fluorescence data showing 3-6 fold increases in somatic markers upon ER stress. Claims C93-C95 demonstrate co-localization between somatic markers and large nuclei, and between somatic markers and engulfed cells. Claim C97 provides a reasonable explanation for incomplete co-localization based on teratoma heterogeneity. The convergence of multiple tissue-specific markers and co-localization data strongly supports transdifferentiation.

results.result: The ectopic somatic cells induced by ER stress in tumorous gonads are derived from germ cells themselves, as demonstrated by their absence in germ cell-deficient glp-1 mutants. This identifies ER stress as a potent regulator of germ cell pluripotency.
results.evaluation: Claim C38 provides critical negative control data showing no ectopic cells in glp-1 mutants lacking germ cells, while control animals show ectopic cells. This lineage-tracing approach definitively establishes germ cell origin. Claims C39-C40 represent reasonable inferences from this data. The experimental design appropriately tests cell origin and the conclusion is well-supported.

results.result: ER stress-induced germ cell transdifferentiation requires the ER stress sensor IRE-1 but is independent of its canonical downstream target XBP-1. Basal transdifferentiation occurs independently of ire-1, but ER stress-induced enhancement is completely ire-1-dependent, indicating an ire-1-dependent, xbp-1-independent signaling pathway.
results.evaluation: Claims C43-C45 show tfg-1 RNAi fails to enhance transdifferentiation in ire-1 mutants while basal levels persist. Claims C46-C48 demonstrate that xbp-1 mutants show enhanced transdifferentiation that is completely ire-1-dependent. This genetic epistasis analysis clearly establishes the pathway hierarchy. The logic is sound and the experimental design appropriately tests the genetic requirements.

results.result: ER stress suppresses the lethal germline tumor in gld-1-deficient animals through enhanced germ cell transdifferentiation coupled with apoptotic clearance of transdifferentiated cells. This suppression is manifested by reduced tumor density, delayed paralysis, and extended lifespan, all requiring ire-1.
results.evaluation: Claims C53-C56 provide multiple independent measures of tumor suppression (density, paralysis, lifespan) with quantitative data. Claim C57 demonstrates ire-1 dependence for all phenotypes, linking tumor suppression to transdifferentiation. Claims C66-C69 synthesize the mechanism. The convergence of multiple physiological readouts, genetic requirements, and mechanistic coherence strongly supports this result.

results.result: Among various cellular stresses that induce germ cell apoptosis in normal germlines (DNA damage, osmotic, mitochondrial, ER stress), only ER stress specifically induces germ cell transdifferentiation and tumor suppression in gld-1-deficient animals. This demonstrates that transdifferentiation is not a general stress response but is specifically associated with ER stress.
results.evaluation: Claims C60 and C62 provide direct comparative experimental data showing only tfg-1 RNAi (ER stress) induces transdifferentiation and tumor suppression, despite other stresses inducing equal or greater apoptosis in normal gonads. This specificity analysis is critical for establishing mechanism. The experimental design appropriately controls for general stress effects and the conclusion is well-justified.

results.result: The gld-1 germline tumor model exhibits key tumorigenic properties including growth factor-independent proliferation, regulation by oncogene/tumor suppressor homologs, acquired apoptosis resistance, and low-frequency spontaneous transdifferentiation that can be enhanced by various genetic manipulations.
results.evaluation: These claims establish the background characteristics of the gld-1 tumor model based on well-cited prior literature (C6-C14). The claims are appropriately supported by citations to established work. This provides essential context for interpreting the current findings but represents prior knowledge rather than new results.

results.result: ER stress can be specifically induced in C. elegans by tunicamycin treatment or tfg-1 RNAi, and promotes germ cell apoptosis in normal germlines. However, gld-1-deficient germ cells are resistant to physiological and DNA damage-induced apoptosis.
results.evaluation: Claims C19-C21 establish the specificity of ER stress induction methods based on prior work and established knowledge. Claims C15-C16 provide context from prior literature. These are well-established facts that provide necessary background but do not represent novel findings of this study.

results.result: Current cancer therapies rely on apoptosis induction but are limited by acquired resistance. Previously identified regulators of germ cell transdifferentiation act at final steps by regulating gene expression, whereas ER stress likely acts upstream, linking physiology to cell fate.
results.evaluation: Claims C4-C5 cite established cancer biology knowledge. Claims C41-C42 compare the current findings to prior work, positioning ER stress as an upstream regulator. While C42 involves some inference about mechanism, it is a reasonable interpretation supported by the genetic data. This provides important context for the significance of the findings.

results.result: The findings parallel observations in mammalian systems where stress responses can benefit cancer outcomes, and relate to human germline tumor biology where 95% of ovarian germline tumors are benign teratomas. The tumor-suppressive properties of IRE-1-related endoribonucleases may be evolutionarily conserved.
results.evaluation: Claims C81-C84 cite clinical literature on human teratomas. Claims C76-C78 discuss RNase L and prostate cancer. While these comparisons are interesting and the citations appear appropriate, the connections are largely speculative (C78, C80, C83, C85). The evolutionary conservation and clinical relevance remain hypotheses requiring direct experimental validation. The reasoning is plausible but not definitively demonstrated.

results.result: Tumor cell transdifferentiation may serve as a protective anti-tumor mechanism with potential therapeutic applications. Transdifferentiation into ectopic cell types may be more effective than same-lineage differentiation by creating niche maladaptation, and could be applied to cancer stem cells in various tissues.
results.evaluation: Claims C87-C89 cite established knowledge about stem cells and differentiation therapy. However, claims C70-C71 and C91-C92 are largely speculative about therapeutic potential. While the C. elegans data support transdifferentiation-mediated tumor suppression in this model, extrapolation to human cancer therapy (C92) requires substantial additional validation. The speculation is reasonable but remains untested.
